Text: Unlike their prokaryotic counterparts, eukaryotic RNA polymerases {{c1::cannot::can or cannot}} initiate transcription by themselves.
Back Extra:
Why: all five eukaryotic RNA polymerases need protein transcription factors, which must bind the promoter and form an initiation complex before the polymerase itself will bind and start the RNA chain.

Distinguish: a prokaryotic RNA polymerase manages initiation itself because its sigma subunit recognizes the promoter and binds the enzyme to it; a eukaryotic polymerase has to wait for separate transcription factors to do that job.

Pitfall: basal transcription factors are required for initiation to happen at all; enhancers and silencers, with still other transcription factors, only modulate how efficiently a promoter initiates.

Text: In a promoter recognized by RNA polymerase II, the conserved element closest to the transcription start site (position +1) is the {{c1::TATA box}}, with consensus sequence {{c1::TATAAAA}} (read 5′ to 3′ on the nontemplate strand) and centered at about position {{c2::−30::position}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the TATA box plays an important role in positioning the transcription startpoint, and it is where the first basal factor, TFIID, binds the promoter, through its TATA-binding protein.

Pitfall: the consensus is written from the nontemplate strand, the strand whose sequence matches the RNA transcript (with T in place of U); the template strand paired with it is the complement, which is why the same box also appears written as ATATTTT.

Text: In an RNA polymerase II promoter, the {{c1::CAAT box}}, consensus sequence {{c1::GGCCAATCT}}, usually occurs near position {{c2::−80::position}}.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: the CAAT and TATA boxes sit at about the same positions in the promoters of most protein-coding nuclear genes, whereas the GC and octamer boxes may be present or absent and turn up at many different locations.

Cue: the box's name sits inside its consensus, GG-CCAAT-CT, so the real recall is the flanking letters.

Distinguish: the TATA and CAAT boxes, by contrast, sit at about the same positions in most protein-coding promoters.

Text:
The first three basal transcription factors to interact with an RNA polymerase II promoter, in order of arrival, are:

1. {{c1::TFIID}}

2. {{c1::TFIIA}}

3. {{c1::TFIIB}}
Back Extra:
Meaning: each basal factor is written TFIIX, Transcription Factor X for RNA polymerase II, where X is a letter identifying the individual factor.

Why: the basal factors must interact with the promoter in the correct sequence for initiation to work; RNA polymerase II does not bind the promoter on its own, only after the factors have begun forming the initiation complex.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: {{c1::TFIID}}, the first basal transcription factor to interact with an RNA polymerase II promoter, contains the {{c2::TATA-binding protein (TBP)}} plus several small proteins associated with it.

Text: After TFIID, TFIIA and TFIIB are in place, the basal transcription factor that joins next is {{c1::TFIIF}}. The same factor first associates with RNA polymerase II so that the two enter the initiation complex together, and one of its two subunits has {{c2::DNA-unwinding}} activity.
Back Extra:
Why: with an unwinding subunit on board, TFIIF probably catalyzes the localized unwinding of the double helix that initiation requires; the polymerase needs a locally unwound segment, with one strand free to serve as template, before it can start.

Distinguish: TFIIH also unwinds DNA, but as the helicase that travels with RNA polymerase II during elongation; TFIIF's unwinding is the local opening of the helix at initiation.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: The basal transcription factor that joins the initiation complex right after TFIIF and RNA polymerase II is {{c1::TFIIE}}, which binds the DNA {{c2::downstream::upstream or downstream}} from the transcription startpoint.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: the promoter's own conserved elements (the TATA, CAAT, GC and octamer boxes) all lie upstream of the startpoint; TFIIE is the factor that binds on the other side, downstream of it.

Pitfall: 'downstream from the startpoint' also describes where most RNA polymerase III promoters sit, inside the transcription unit; for RNA polymerase II it describes where TFIIE binds, not where the promoter is.

Roster: TFIID → TFIIA → TFIIB → TFIIF (bringing RNA polymerase II) → TFIIE → TFIIH and TFIIJ.

Text: The basal transcription factor {{c1::TFIIH}} has {{c2::helicase}} activity, used alongside RNA polymerase II during {{c3::elongation::initiation or elongation}}.
